bifrost: bifrost_app::keychain (springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs), springboard/src/keychain.rs, springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (KeychainOp), springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs, springboard/src/shell/update.rs, springboard/src/shell/sha256.rs, springboard/sdk/src/url.rs, springboard/src/privd/auth.rs, springboard/src/shell/passcode.rs
summary: BifrOSt covers generic-password keychain items for apps (asynchronous, per-app store), app sandboxing, login authentication and HTTPS transport for the shell. It has no SDK API for code signing, certificate trust evaluation, Authorization Services, or the SecRandom and crypto transform calls, and it has no code signing or notarization at all.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete); springboard/src/keychain.rs; springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (KeychainOp, KeychainStatus)
features.note: Only generic passwords, keyed by (service, account). Errors mirror OSStatus codes. No internet-password, certificate, key or identity classes, no access groups, no iCloud sync. Calls are asynchronous, unlike Apple's synchronous calls (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Keychain section).

features.apple: Keychain data protection classes and Secure Enclave-backed keys
features.bifrost: springboard/src/keychain.rs (BKC1 file, ChaCha20 plus HMAC-SHA256, per-app subkeys)
features.note: Encrypted per app with a master key stored beside the items. No TPM or login-password key source yet, so it does not protect against root or a whole-disk attacker. Apps get no SDK option to choose a protection class.

Fail-closed bubblewrap sandbox driven by manifest permissions, with a separate app account and cgroups. Apps have no SDK API that reads or changes their sandbox state. Apple's entitlement model is not used.

Wave 2 (theme-01, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The privileged helper (privd) checks login through PAM for the shell. Apps have no authorization API, and the manifest permission is the only grant. docs/bifrost-ui.md records that the shell still runs as root (stage 2 is pending).

features.bifrost: springboard/src/privd/auth.rs; springboard/src/shell/passcode.rs (salted, stretched SHA-256 passcode with lockout)
features.note: Login is a PAM check with lockout backoff; the passcode is stored hashed with a lockout deadline. No app-facing LocalAuthentication-style prompt was found in the SDK.
Apps get HTTPS through the shell's rustls stack. No SDK API to set or inspect the trust policy, pin certificates or read the peer certificate.

Wave 3 (theme-10, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The Wi-Fi 802.1X sheet has a Don't Validate Server option, but that is a user choice in the network sheet, not a certificate API (springboard/src/shell/wifi_page.rs:56, NOTICE). The SDK has no certificate types.
The shell's update client is HTTPS only. The SDK URL client uses rustls by default. No manifest-level ATS-style exception list or policy for apps.

features.apple: Code signing checks during Mac software updates (Updating Mac Software)
features.note: Updates are checked by SHA-256 against the manifest, which is not signed. update.rs states that TLS authenticates the server and there is no client-side manifest signature, so an attacker who controls the manifest controls the hash.
No code signing or signature verification found in the repo. Apps are installed without a signature check (store apps run from /var/lib/springboard/apps/<id>).

features.apple: Notarizing macOS software before distribution; Hardened Runtime
features.note: Apple's notary service has no BifrOSt counterpart. The Linux sandbox in app_policy.rs covers the same goal, but it is not a Hardened Runtime.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/keychain.rs, springboard/src/shell/passcode.rs and springboard/src/privd/auth.rs use the OS random source internally
features.note: No SDK call returns random bytes to apps. Internal use only.
No SDK API for encryption, signing or key objects. Hashing and MAC are internal to the shell.

features.feature: Password AutoFill and Shared Web Credentials
features.note: Depends on Apple's iCloud Keychain and associated domains. No BifrOSt counterpart.

Wave 3 (theme-28, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK text-field content type for one-time codes or autofill from messages.

features.apple: OSStatus values such as errSecDuplicateItem and errSecItemNotFound
features.note: Only the keychain errors are mirrored. Other Security OSStatus values have no counterpart.

features.feature: Legacy Secure Transport, Secure Download, CSSM
features.apple: Secure Transport, Secure Download, Common Security Services Manager
features.note: Deprecated Apple interfaces. No BifrOSt counterpart is needed.

gaps: Certificate and trust evaluation API (SecTrust, SecPolicy, SecIdentity) for apps; the SDK has no certificate types
Code signing and signature verification for apps and updates; the update manifest is not signed
Authorization Services: an app-facing authorization API for privileged operations
Randomization API (SecRandomCopyBytes equivalent) in the SDK
Key objects and crypto transforms (encrypt, sign, verify) in the SDK
Keychain item classes beyond generic passwords, access groups, and data protection classes
Keychain master key is on the same disk as the items (no TPM or login-password key source)
One-time code text content type for autofill
Synchronous keychain calls (Apple's are synchronous; BifrOSt's are asynchronous by design)
